newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore home loan move to shorten queue - Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: Singapore home loan move to shorten queue - Fin Min.

text.p: Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Sunday that new credit tightening measures for public housing were designed to shorten queues for genuine buyers.

Singapore on Saturday ended government-subsidised housing loans for those with incomes over Singapore $8,000 ($5,555) per month, and limited the number of subsidised housing loans for most home buyers to just two in a lifetime.
Public housing in Singapore is provided by the Housing Development Board (HDB).
"The HDB new credit tightening measures for HDB flats will benefit genuine buyers by shortening queues for flats and resale flats," Hu said in an interview broadcast on state television.
"Therefore it should be beneficial for all first time HDB buyers, and for upgraders who actually need the extra space," he said.
Around 86 percent of Singaporeans live in flats built by the government, and about 90 percent of these flats are owned by the people who live in them.
Under the government's housing subsidy, public sector home buyers pay just 3.58 percent for a mortgage loan against the 6.75 to seven percent the major banks charge for loans of up to 30 years.
